new:
[F8] Every Cauchy sequence of real numbers converges to a real number, and
$\mathbb R$ is a complete totally ordered field: every nonempty subset of
$\mathbb R$ bounded above has a real supremum. Both conclusions are established
without a choice principle by [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]]. The terminology
"complete ordered field" and "supremum" is defined in
[[def-complete-ordered-field]]; that definition alone is not an existence result.

Its convergence follows from [F8], and the same uniform tail estimate gives that limit for all real radii tending to infinity. new:
[F7] Every nonempty bounded-above subset of the Cauchy-sequence real field
has a real least upper bound, as established by
[[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]. This is the real field used here;
[[def-complete-ordered-field]] supplies the terminology rather than proving
that property for $\mathbb R$.
The set $\{A_R(V):R>0\}$ is nonempty (take $R=1$) and bounded above, so its finite real supremum $A(V)$ exists by [F7].
